title: Lower central dark matter densities in nearby galaxies than predicted by simulations - Nature Astronomy
byline: Lei; Yu; Zhu; Ling; Yang; Meng; Despali; Giulia; Zheng; Ran; Xu; Dandan; Niankun; Falcón-Barroso; Jesús; Jiang; Fangzhou; Van De Ven; Glenn; Wang; Jie
html:
Abstract

Baryonic feedback in hydrodynamical simulations is typically invoked to alleviate the core–cusp problem in dwarf galaxies. Yet baryonic processes also induce adiabatic contraction of dark matter (DM), producing overly steep density profiles and excessively high DM fractions in the inner regions of massive galaxies. The DM distribution of galaxies across a wide stellar mass range is therefore a critical test for such simulations, but a comprehensive benchmark has remained absent. Here we consistently measure the DM distribution from galaxy centres out to radii of 20–50 kpc for 136 nearby galaxies that together span the local mass–size relation over the stellar mass interval 109–1011.5 M⊙. We identify central regions with lower DM densities relative to Λ cold dark matter simulation expectations, whose extent grows from about 10 to >50 kpc as stellar mass increases from 1010 to 1011 M⊙. Although their physical origin remains unclear, these low-dark-matter regions are clearly indicated by the data. Our results provide an important observational benchmark for future hydrodynamical simulations that explore alternative DM models and feedback processes.

Data availability

The MaNGA data used in this work are publicly available from the SDSS data archive at https://www.sdss4.org/dr17/manga/manga-data/data-access/. The CALIFA data products are publicly available from the CALIFA survey archive at http://califa.caha.es/. The pPXF-based stellar-population products for the MaNGA subsample are available from the DynPop project via Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15742824 (ref. 120); the CALIFA stellar-population products are available from the CALIFA V500 pyPipe3D data release at https://ifs.astroscu.unam.mx/CALIFA/V500/v2.3/pyPipe3D/. The integrated H i spectra were obtained from the HI-MaNGA survey at https://www.sdss4.org/dr17/manga/hi-manga/, archival single-dish H i measurements through the NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database at https://ned.ipac.caltech.edu/ and FAST observations carried out as part of this work (PT2023_0024; PI: Ling Zhu). The reduced FAST spectra are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. The derived quantities supporting the main results of this study, including the inferred stellar, DM and total mass of the 136 galaxies, are provided as Supplementary Data 1.

Code availability

The FAST reduction pipeline is available at https://github.com/NiankunYu/ALMaQUEST_FAST-HI2024. The stellar dynamical modelling was carried out with the publicly available DYNAMITE package95,100,101, available at https://github.com/dynamics-of-stellar-systems/dynamite.
